summary: ORBITAL is a self-check health console for astronauts on long-duration missions. Crew members enter daily readings such as heart rate, blood pressure, glucose, temperature, sleep, radiation dose, hydration, food intake, mood and exercise. They see a color-coded readiness score, trend charts, a clickable body map and plain-language guidance on what to do and when to contact a flight surgeon. It matters because on Moon and Mars missions ground medical help is delayed, so crews must assess their own health.
details:
ORBITAL is a browser-based self-check health console for astronauts on long-duration missions (station, transit, Moon and Mars), where help from Earth is delayed or unavailable.

What it does: crew members enter their own readings in a daily check-in. ORBITAL shows 11 indicators with green, amber or red status and trend charts against expected ranges. A clickable body map links each region to its indicators. Hazard cards turn indicator status into Low, Moderate or High risk for the five hazards of human spaceflight (radiation, isolation, distance from Earth, gravity fields, and hostile closed environments). Each measurement comes with plain-language guidance and clear signs of when to contact a flight surgeon. Scheduled checks cover weekly mass, eye and skin photos, bone-loading review and support calls. Streaks, XP and badges encourage routine self-care.

How it works: the crew member types in readings, ORBITAL classifies each one, explains why it matters in space and suggests actions. Photo checks compare redness between two photos on the device only and are not a diagnosis. Entries are stored only in the user’s browser. Sample data is clearly labeled and separate from real entries.

Limits: all readings are entered by the user, and the tool connects to no medical hardware. Reference ranges are general adult guides, not medical advice. Flight surgeons set personal limits.

Next steps: import from approved onboard devices, per-crew limits, offline use with secure sync to ground, and testing with flight-medicine experts.

Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single page, browser local storage, the Inter font, and GitHub Pages for hosting.
